ASSISTANT: Congratulations on your new home! I'm Robert from First National Bank. What's your loan number?
USER: FNB-789456123.
ASSISTANT: Perfect, Mr. Brian Foster. Your loan for 487 Maple Drive closed February 12th.
USER: Right. Purchase price was $625,000?
ASSISTANT: Correct. You put down 20%, which is $125,000.
USER: And my loan amount?
ASSISTANT: Your mortgage is $500,000 at 6.75% for 30 years.
USER: What's my monthly payment?
ASSISTANT: Principal and interest is $3,243. With taxes and insurance, total is $4,285.
USER: Break that down for me?
ASSISTANT: P&I $3,243, property tax $708, homeowners insurance $234, PMI is zero since you put 20% down.
USER: The property tax seems high.
ASSISTANT: Annual property tax is $8,500. That's about 1.36% of purchase price.
USER: Is that all deductible?
ASSISTANT: Yes, property tax is deductible up to $10,000 combined with state taxes.
USER: What about the mortgage interest?
ASSISTANT: Mortgage interest is fully deductible on loans up to $750,000.
USER: How much interest will I pay this year?
ASSISTANT: For 2024, approximately $31,000 since you're starting in February.
USER: That's a lot of interest.
ASSISTANT: Yes, early years are mostly interest. First payment is $450 principal, $2,793 interest.
USER: When's my first payment due?
ASSISTANT: April 1st, 2024. We skip March since you closed mid-February.
USER: Did I pay points on this loan?
ASSISTANT: Yes, you paid 1.5 points to buy down the rate, that's $7,500.
USER: Are points tax deductible?
ASSISTANT: Yes, points paid on a purchase mortgage are fully deductible in the year paid.
USER: Good. What about closing costs?
ASSISTANT: Total closing costs were $14,750 including points.
USER: What else was in there?
ASSISTANT: Origination fee $5,000, title insurance $1,200, appraisal $650, attorney $1,400.
USER: Can I deduct those?
ASSISTANT: Only the points. Other closing costs are added to your home's cost basis.
USER: Cost basis?
ASSISTANT: For future sale calculations. Your basis is $625,000 purchase plus $7,250 non-deductible closing costs.
USER: So $632,250 total basis?
ASSISTANT: Correct. Important for capital gains when you eventually sell.
USER: I plan to live here long-term.
ASSISTANT: Good! Primary residence gets $250,000 capital gains exclusion, $500,000 if married.
USER: I'm married. Speaking of which, we're filing jointly.
ASSISTANT: Then you can deduct all the mortgage interest and property taxes on your joint return.
USER: Will you send me the tax forms?
ASSISTANT: Yes, Form 1098 by January 31st showing interest paid and points.
USER: What if I make extra principal payments?
ASSISTANT: No prepayment penalty. Extra payments reduce principal and lifetime interest.
USER: I'm thinking of paying an extra $500 monthly.
ASSISTANT: That would save you $287,000 in interest and pay off the loan 9 years early.
USER: Wow! Maybe I'll do that after settling in.
ASSISTANT: Smart thinking. Get comfortable with the payment first.
USER: Is my escrow account set up?
ASSISTANT: Yes, we collect for property tax and insurance monthly.
USER: Initial escrow balance?
ASSISTANT: You deposited $2,834 at closing for initial escrow cushion.
USER: When do you pay the insurance?
ASSISTANT: Annual premium due February 1st each year, we'll pay from escrow.
USER: And property taxes?
ASSISTANT: Due in two installments - April and November in your county.
USER: You handle both?
ASSISTANT: Yes, we pay from your escrow account. You'll get an annual escrow analysis.
USER: What if there's a shortage?
ASSISTANT: We'll adjust your monthly payment or you can pay the shortage lump sum.
USER: Hopefully taxes don't go up too much.
ASSISTANT: There's usually a homestead exemption. Have you applied?
USER: Not yet. How do I do that?
ASSISTANT: County assessor's office. Can save you $500-1000 annually on taxes.
USER: I'll do that right away.
ASSISTANT: File by March 31st for this tax year.
USER: Thanks for reminding me. Anything else I should know?
ASSISTANT: Keep all documentation for taxes. Your CPA will need the closing statement.
USER: I have everything in a folder.
ASSISTANT: Perfect. Congratulations again on your new home!
USER: Thanks for all your help!
ASSISTANT: My pleasure. Call if you need anything, Mr. Foster.

ASSISTANT: You have 500 shares of Apple, currently at $185 per share, total value $92,500.
USER: What did I pay for them?
ASSISTANT: You have multiple purchase lots. 200 shares bought in 2018 at $45, 300 shares in 2020 at $75.
USER: So if I sell all of them?
ASSISTANT: Your cost basis is $31,500 total. Selling at $92,500 means $61,000 capital gain.
USER: That's a big tax hit.
ASSISTANT: Yes, but it's all long-term capital gains since you've held over a year.
USER: What's the tax rate on that?
ASSISTANT: Depends on your income. Could be 0%, 15%, or 20% federal, plus state taxes.
USER: I make about $125,000 a year.
ASSISTANT: Married filing jointly?
USER: Yes, my wife makes about $85,000.
ASSISTANT: So $210,000 combined. You'd likely pay 15% federal capital gains tax.
USER: That's $9,150 on the gain?
ASSISTANT: Correct, plus your state tax. What state are you in?
USER: California.
ASSISTANT: California taxes capital gains as ordinary income, so could be another 9.3%.
USER: Ouch. Maybe I should sell less?
ASSISTANT: How much do you need for the improvements?
USER: About $50,000.
ASSISTANT: You could sell just 300 shares for $55,500, keep taxes lower.
USER: Which shares should I sell for best tax treatment?
ASSISTANT: Specific lot identification. Sell the 300 shares from 2020 at $75 cost basis.
USER: Why those?
ASSISTANT: Higher cost basis means lower gain. $55,500 proceeds minus $22,500 basis equals $33,000 gain.
USER: Much better than $61,000 gain.
ASSISTANT: Exactly. Federal tax about $4,950, California about $3,069.
USER: So roughly $8,000 total tax?
ASSISTANT: Yes, approximately. Versus $15,000+ if you sold everything.
USER: Let's do that. Sell the 300 shares from 2020.
ASSISTANT: Market order or limit?
USER: What's it trading at now?
ASSISTANT: $185.25 currently.
USER: Market order is fine.
ASSISTANT: Executing now... Filled at $185.30. Proceeds $55,590.
USER: Perfect. When will funds be available?
ASSISTANT: Trade settles in 2 business days, so June 24th.
USER: Can you transfer to my checking?
ASSISTANT: Yes, Chase account ending in 4782?
USER: That's the one.
ASSISTANT: Transfer will complete June 25th.
USER: What about estimated taxes?
ASSISTANT: You should make an estimated tax payment for Q2 by June 15th.
USER: I missed that deadline.
ASSISTANT: Pay as soon as possible. Q3 deadline is September 15th.
USER: How much should I pay?
ASSISTANT: Roughly $8,000 for federal and state on this gain.
USER: I'll do that. Will I get a 1099?
ASSISTANT: Yes, 1099-B in January showing proceeds and cost basis.
USER: Good for tax prep. What about the remaining Apple shares?
ASSISTANT: You still have 200 shares worth about $37,000.
USER: I'll hold those for now.
ASSISTANT: Smart to keep some exposure to Apple. It's been a great performer.
USER: Any other tax considerations?
ASSISTANT: The home improvements might increase your home's cost basis.
USER: Really? Which improvements qualify?
ASSISTANT: Capital improvements like new kitchen, bathroom, additions. Not repairs or maintenance.
USER: I'm doing a kitchen remodel and adding a deck.
ASSISTANT: Both should qualify. Keep receipts and documentation.
USER: Will do. Thanks for the tax-efficient sale strategy!
ASSISTANT: You're welcome! Saved you about $7,000 in taxes.

ASSISTANT: Exactly! You save capital gains tax on $18,000.
